claims: The Automated Ball-Strike (ABS) Challenge System starts with the 2026 MLB season.
The ABS Challenge System allows players to immediately appeal home plate umpire calls.
Players (pitcher, catcher, or batter) challenge by tapping their helmet/hat.
Tapping their helmet/hat prompts a Hawkeye-camera replay.
Teams start with two challenges per game, as ESPN states.
Successful challenges lead to no loss of a challenge, as ESPN states.
If a challenge is initiated, the pitch is immediately replayed.
The replay shows the precise location relative to the batter's specific height-calibrated strike zone.
The replay is shown on the stadium scoreboard.
Only the batter, pitcher, or catcher can initiate a challenge within seconds of the call, says Facebook.
The ABS Challenge System was extensively tested in Minor League Baseball before the 2026 MLB season implementation, says Netflix.
The ABS Challenge System was extensively tested in MLB Spring Training before the 2026 MLB season implementation, says Netflix.
